text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Rem Vyakhirev, newly reelected head of Gazprom, remains one of the most influential figures in Russia's economic and political life.
- Average Russians spend 21 percent of their income on buying hard currency.
- Import taxes for packaged coffee may grow considerably in the near future, according to the importers.
- President Boris Yeltsin is likely to spend his July holidays either in the central Samara region or in Karelia in the northwest.
- A 28-year old drunken businessman hit the base of Lenin's mausoleum in Red Square over the weekend.
- Moscow car producer AZLK is planning a new type of middle range vehicle together with VAZ, Russia's biggest car maker.
- A "safe sex is my choice" television campaign will be launched in Moscow in the near future.
- Deputy Prime Minister Valery Serov, a strong supporter of Russia-Belarus union, is likely to represent Russia at the NATO countries' meeting in Madrid.
- Police confiscated about pirate 20,000 CD roms, worth one million dollars from a 24-year old businessman near Moscow.
